# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stateless failure diagnosis for cross-key append proofs: a companion to
# check_rhe that reports every failing rotation-chain hop and both endpoint
# root signatures rather than a bare False. The rotation-chain checks reuse
# the anchor / link / authorization semantics of diagnose_rotation_chain,
# and the two endpoint signatures are always re-verified independently, so a
# broken chain never masks a bad root signature. The diagnosis only locates
# failing checks on public data; it never guesses at an attacker. No state
# is kept and check_rhe's short-circuiting behaviour is left unchanged.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RHEFault:
    """One failing check located while diagnosing a cross-key append proof.

    The fields, in order, are ``check`` (the check that failed) and
    ``index`` (the zero-based rotation-chain certificate position pinned to
    the failure, or ``None``). The stable, never-confused ``check`` values
    are:

    - ``"anchor"`` — the rotation chain anchor differs from the first
      certificate's ``old``; always at index 0.
    - ``"link"`` — the certificate immediately before ``index`` has a
      ``new`` that differs from the certificate at ``index``'s ``old``.
    - ``"authorization"`` — the certificate at ``index`` is structurally
      legal but :func:`verify_rotation` rejects its signature.
    - ``"old-signature"`` — the old endpoint's root signature does not
      verify on ``b"sh/r" || U64(old_total) || old_root`` under the first
      certificate's group parameters and ``old`` key; ``index`` is None.
    - ``"new-signature"`` — the new endpoint's root signature does not
      verify on ``b"sh/r" || U64(n) || new_root`` under the last
      certificate's group parameters and ``new`` key; ``index`` is None.

    The dataclass is frozen, positionally constructible and compared by
    value, and carries no network, storage or hidden state.
    """

    check: str
    index: int | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RHEDiagnosis:
    """Every failing chain and endpoint-signature check of an :class:`RHE`.

    ``valid`` is the verdict — ``True`` exactly when :func:`check_rhe`
    returns ``True`` for the same proof — and ``faults`` the non-None tuple
    of every :class:`RHEFault` found. The rotation-chain faults come first
    in certificate order: walking the certificates by their zero-based
    index, each position's positional fault (``"anchor"`` at index 0,
    ``"link"`` elsewhere, when present) precedes that position's
    ``"authorization"`` fault, and a position may carry both because each
    certificate signature is checked independently of the linkage. After
    the chain faults come ``"old-signature"`` and then ``"new-signature"``,
    each at most once and both with ``index`` None; the endpoint root
    signatures are re-verified independently of one another and of the
    chain, so a broken chain never masks a bad root signature. No fault is
    reported for an honest single- or multi-hop proof:
    ``RHEDiagnosis(True, ())``.

    Like a bare :class:`RHE`, the dataclass is frozen, positionally
    constructible and compared by value, keeps no network, storage or
    hidden state, and never infers an attacker from a mismatch.
    """

    valid: bool
    faults: tuple[RHEFault, ...]


def diagnose_rhe(x: RHE) -> RHEDiagnosis:
    """Locate every failing chain hop and endpoint signature of an RHE.

    The stateless companion of :func:`check_rhe`: the returned
    :class:`RHEDiagnosis`'s ``valid`` field is always exactly the boolean
    :func:`check_rhe` returns for the same proof, but a failing diagnosis
    additionally pinpoints every check that does not hold instead of
    folding them into one ``False``. The extension, rotation chain,
    certificates and both signatures are structurally validated up front
    with exactly the boundary of :func:`check_rhe`, and every signature's
    integers are additionally range-checked against the endpoint group
    they are actually verified under, so the checks below only ever run on
    structurally legal values and deterministic input damage is never
    dressed up as a diagnostic fault.

    Scanning the certificates in chain order, three stable
    ``check`` values can appear, with the same semantics as
    :func:`diagnose_rotation_chain`:

    - ``"anchor"`` — ``rotations.anchor`` differs from the first
      certificate's ``old``; reported once at index 0.
    - ``"link"`` — for an adjacent pair, ``certificates[i].new`` differs
      from ``certificates[i + 1].old``; reported at index ``i + 1``.
    - ``"authorization"`` — a structurally legal certificate whose
      :func:`verify_rotation` signature check returns ``False``; reported
      at the certificate's own index.

    Afterwards the two endpoint root statements are rebuilt from
    ``x.extension`` with the ordinary seal-history tree rules (the first
    ``old_total`` leaves give the old root and all leaves the new one),
    and the root signatures are checked independently even when the chain
    is broken: ``"old-signature"`` is reported when ``x.old_sig`` fails on
    ``b"sh/r" || U64(old_total) || old_root`` under the first
    certificate's ``(q, p, g, old)``, and ``"new-signature"`` when
    ``x.new_sig`` fails on ``b"sh/r" || U64(n) || new_root`` under the
    last certificate's ``(q, p, g, new)``; both carry ``index`` None.

    Every observable failure is collected in one pass: one bad hop or
    endpoint never masks another, the same index may carry both a
    positional and an ``"authorization"`` fault, and a tampered old or new
    root signature, a swapped signature pair, a broken rotation
    authorization or a severed key link each pinpoints its own failure.
    With no failing check the fault tuple is empty and ``valid`` is
    ``True``; otherwise ``valid`` is ``False``. Equal inputs always yield
    equal, deterministically ordered reports.

    A non-:class:`RHE` argument or wrong field types raise TypeError,
    exactly as :func:`check_rhe`. An empty rotation chain, an
    ``old_total`` of zero or at least the leaf count, an empty leaf set or
    a leaf that is not exactly 32 bytes, a structurally illegal chain
    certificate or aggregate signature, or a signature whose integers do
    not fit the corresponding endpoint's parameters raise ValueError,
    exactly as :func:`check_rhe` and :func:`verify_signature` do. A
    structurally legal proof whose chain, links or signatures do not match
    cryptographically returns a report normally and never raises. The
    function is stateless, neither infers an attacker nor mutates
    :func:`check_rhe`'s short-circuiting behaviour, and keeps no hidden
    state.
    """
    _extension, rotations, old_sig, new_sig, old_total, leaves = (
        _check_rhe_fields(x)
    )

    # Full structural validation of every certificate up front, along the
    # same boundary diagnose_rotation_chain relies on, so the scan below
    # only ever sees structurally legal certificates and a failing
    # signature is a cryptographic mismatch, never malformed input.
    for cert in rotations.certificates:
        _check_rotation_fields(
            cert.old, cert.new, cert.ids, cert.t, cert.q, cert.p, cert.g, cert.sig
        )
    first = rotations.certificates[0]
    last = rotations.certificates[-1]
    # Each root signature is range-checked against the endpoint group it
    # is actually verified under; check_rhe reaches verify_signature only
    # through a fully verified chain, whose bounds guarantee this.
    _check_signature_against_endpoint(old_sig, first.q, first.p)
    _check_signature_against_endpoint(new_sig, last.q, last.p)

    faults: list[RHEFault] = []
    for index, cert in enumerate(rotations.certificates):
        if index == 0:
            if rotations.anchor != cert.old:
                faults.append(RHEFault("anchor", 0))
        elif rotations.certificates[index - 1].new != cert.old:
            faults.append(RHEFault("link", index))
        if not verify_rotation(cert):
            faults.append(RHEFault("authorization", index))

    old_root = _history_extension_root(leaves[:old_total])
    new_root = _history_extension_root(leaves)
    old_message = (
        SEAL_HISTORY_PROOF_ROOT_TAG + _history_proof_u64(old_total) + old_root
    )
    new_message = (
        SEAL_HISTORY_PROOF_ROOT_TAG
        + _history_proof_u64(len(leaves))
        + new_root
    )

    if not verify_signature(
        old_message,
        old_sig,
        first.old,
        group_prime=first.p,
        generator=first.g,
        prime=first.q,
    ):
        faults.append(RHEFault("old-signature", None))
    if not verify_signature(
        new_message,
        new_sig,
        last.new,
        group_prime=last.p,
        generator=last.g,
        prime=last.q,
    ):
        faults.append(RHEFault("new-signature", None))

    return RHEDiagnosis(not faults, tuple(faults))


def _check_signature_against_endpoint(
    signature: AggregateSignature, prime: int, group_prime: int

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RHEFault:
    """One failing check located while diagnosing a cross-key append proof.

    The fields, in order, are ``check`` (the check that failed) and
    ``index`` (the zero-based rotation-chain certificate position pinned to
    the failure, or ``None``). The stable, never-confused ``check`` values
    are:

    - ``"anchor"`` — the rotation chain anchor differs from the first
      certificate's ``old``; always at index 0.
    - ``"link"`` — the certificate immediately before ``index`` has a
      ``new`` that differs from the certificate at ``index``'s ``old``.
    - ``"authorization"`` — the certificate at ``index`` is structurally
      legal but :func:`verify_rotation` rejects its signature.
    - ``"old-signature"`` — the old endpoint's root signature does not
      verify on ``b"sh/r" || U64(old_total) || old_root`` under the first
      certificate's group parameters and ``old`` key; ``index`` is None.
    - ``"new-signature"`` — the new endpoint's root signature does not
      verify on ``b"sh/r" || U64(n) || new_root`` under the last
      certificate's group parameters and ``new`` key; ``index`` is None.

    value, and carries no network, storage or hidden state.

    index: int | None

    ``"link"`` elsewhere, when present) precedes that position's

    certificate signature is checked independently of the linkage. After

    each at most once and both with ``index`` None; the endpoint root

content.text:
Done. I added the locatable cross-key append-proof diagnosis as a pure extension of the public API, without touching any existing entry point.

## What was added

**`thresholdsign/__init__.py`** (3 new public symbols, exported in `__all__` and the module docstring):

- **`RHEFault(check, index)`** — frozen, positional value type. `check` ∈ `"anchor"`, `"link"`, `"authorization"` (carrying the zero-based certificate index, same semantics as `RotationFault`) or `"old-signature"`, `"new-signature"` (root-signature failures with `index=None`). Field order is `(check, index)` per the spec.
- **`RHEDiagnosis(valid, faults)`** — frozen value type with `(valid, faults)`.
- **`diagnose_rhe(x) -> RHEDiagnosis`** — stateless companion to `check_rhe`. It:
  - structurally validates the extension, chain, every certificate and both signatures **up front on exactly `check_rhe`'s boundary** (via `_check_rhe_fields` + `_check_rotation_fields`), so deterministic damage raises, never masquerades as a fault;
  - additionally pre-range-checks each root signature against the endpoint group it is actually verified under (`_check_signature_against_endpoint`, including the order-q subgroup check on `R`) — necessary because `diagnose_rhe` reaches `verify_signature` even when the chain is broken, where `check_rhe` short-circuits;
  - walks certificates in order, reporting `anchor`/`link` before `authorization` at each position (both may appear), then independently re-verifies the old and new endpoint root signatures — **even if the chain is broken** — appending `old-signature` then `new-signature`;
  - collects every observable failure in one pass, never inferring an attacker. `valid` is exactly `not faults` and matches `check_rhe`'s truth value; equal inputs give equal, ordered reports.

**`tests/test_diagnose_rhe.py`** — 32 tests: result shape/field order/frozen equality, honest single- and multi-hop proofs, each fault type in isolation, same-index ordering, broken-chain + both-bad-signatures (proving endpoints are checked independently), swapped pair, severed link, tampered leaves/roots, full-fault ordering, determinism, and the complete TypeError/ValueError boundary (including an out-of-endpoint-range `z` and a non-subgroup `R` with a broken chain). Tests cross-assert `diagnosis.valid == check_rhe(x)`.

**`README.md`** — API entries for the three new symbols in the existing Chinese documentation style.

## Verification

- New module: 32 tests pass.
- Full suite: **3943 tests, OK** (ran twice against final code); no existing entry point, return value, exception boundary or canonical encoding changed.
- Additional randomized cross-check over 12 mutated proofs confirmed `valid` agreement and fault-ordering invariants.
